Rashi on Shabbat 147a:10:1.hebrew: נשאל איתמר - לא אירע מעשה זה לרבי, אלא שאלו לפניו מהו לצאת בו, ובקש להתיר, עד שאמרו לפניו משום רבי מאיר: חייב חטאת. דאיהו סבר הואיל ואינה מקופלת — שהרי אחוריה היו נופלין למטה מן כתפיו, אלא שצידיה היו מונחים על כתפיו — הוה סבר דרך מלבוש הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:10:1.english: It was stated [that he] was asked - This incident did not happen to Rabbi [himself]; rather, they asked before him: What is [the law regarding] going out with it [on Shabbat]? And he sought to permit [it], until they said before him in the name of Rabbi Meir: [One is] liable [for] a sin-offering. For he [Rabbi] reasoned: since it is not folded up — for its back was falling down below his shoulders, and only its sides were resting on his shoulders — he thought [that] it is a [normal] manner of wearing [a garment].

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:11:1.hebrew: מי מערה - מי מקוה מקורה שהוא חם ואין חומו יוצא, ודוקא חמין נקט, ומש"ה קתני "הרוחץ", דיעבד:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:11:1.english: Cave water - Water of a roofed mikveh that is hot and whose heat does not escape. It specifically mentions hot [water], and therefore it teaches "one who bathes," [implying] after the fact.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:11:3.hebrew: אפי' בעשר אלונטיות - סדינין שמקנחין בהן, וסיפג בהן זה אחר זה. ורבותא היא דלא נפישי מיא בכל חד, אפ"ה לא יביאם בידו בתוך ביתו, אפי' ע"י עירוב, שמא ישכח ויסחט בבואו:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:11:3.english: Even with ten towels - Sheets with which people dry themselves, and he dried himself with them one after another. And it is a novel point, for there is not much water in each one; nevertheless, he may not bring them in his hand into his house, even by means of an eruv, lest he forget and wring [them] out when he arrives.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:11:4.hebrew: אבל עשרה בני אדם - הואיל ומרובין הן, מדכרי אהדדי:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:11:4.english: But ten people - Since they are many, they remind one another [not to wring it out].

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:11:5.hebrew: מסתפגין באלונטית אחת - והיינו נמי רבותא, דחדא אלונטית לעשרה נפישא ביה מיא, אפילו הכי מביאין אותה בידים:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:11:5.english: Dry [themselves] with one towel - And this too is a novelty: that [with] one towel for ten [people], there is much water in it; even so, they may carry it in [their] hands.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:11:6.hebrew: פניהם ידיהם ורגליהם - אורחא דמילתא נקט, וה"ה לכל גופם:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:11:6.english: Their faces, their hands, and their feet - [The Mishnah] stated the usual case, and the same applies to their entire body.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:1.english: One may anoint - [with] oil on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:10.english: He may not agitate them - [This is] the terminology of beaten eggs in a bowl (Chullin 64a).

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:2.english: And [one may] rub - with the hand over the entire body for pleasure.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:3.english: However, one may not exert oneself - [Meaning] to rub forcefully.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:4.hebrew: ולא מתגררין - גרסינן, במגררת שקורין אשטרייל"א, דהוי עובדא דחול:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:4.english: And one may not scrape - We read [the text as velo mitgarerin]; [it refers to scraping] with a scraper that they call estrille [strigil], for it is a weekday activity.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:5.hebrew: לקורדימא - שם הנהר, ובגמ' מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:5.english: Into Kurdima - The name of the river, and in the Gemara [it] explains the reason.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:7.hebrew: ואין מעצבין את הקטן - לשון "ידיך עצבוני" (איוב י׳:ח׳), שמתקנים ומיישבין עצמותיו וחוליות שדרתו כמדת צלמו, ובגמרא אמר טעמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:7.english: And one may not shape [align] the infant - [This is] an expression [akin to] "Your hands shaped me" (Job 10:8), for they adjust and straighten his bones and the vertebrae of his spine according to the proportion of his form; and in the Gemara it states the reason.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:8.english: And one may not reset a break - A bone that was broken. All medical treatment is forbidden [on Shabbat] due to [the concern of] grinding herbs.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:9.hebrew: נפרקה - אלויישי"ר בלעז, שיצא העצם מפרק שלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:12:9.english: Was dislocated - Aloisher in Old French, [meaning] that the bone came out of its joint.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:1:1.english: One who shakes his cloak - [Shaking it] from dust.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:1:2.english: [He is] liable [to bring] a sin-offering - For this is its laundering.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:1:3.english: Only with black [garments] - For the dust spoils its appearance and he is particular about it.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:1:4.english: And this [applies only] when he is particular about them - [not] to wear them until he shakes them out.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:2:1.english: They are desecrating Shabbat - And they were black cloaks.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:2:2.hebrew: לא קפדינן - לא איכפת לן אם יש עליה אבק, הלכך לאו ליבון הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:2:2.english: We are not particular - We do not care if there is dust on it; therefore, it is not [considered] laundering.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:3:2.english: He was hesitating [hava ka mechasem] - [This is] an expression [related to] "You shall not muzzle [lo tachsom]" (Deuteronomy 25).

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:3:3.english: To give [it] to him - For it is necessary to shake the dew off it.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:4:1.hebrew: בטלית מקופלת - לאחר שנתנה על ראשו, הגביה שיפוליה על כתפיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:4:1.english: With a folded cloak - After he placed it on his head, he lifted its lower edges onto his shoulders.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:4:2.english: Liable [to bring] a sin-offering - For this is not a manner of wearing [a garment].

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:5:1.english: And the Ratanin - [They are so called] after the name of a place.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:6:1.english: A thread wound around his finger - So that [the scarf] would not fall from his shoulders.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:7:3.hebrew: כיסוי בבלייתא - שמסלקין בגדיהם מן הארץ כשהן ארוכין, וכופלין אותו כלפי מעלה — פרונצי"ש (קפלים) — ומחזיקין אותן ע"י חוטין, והיינו כמין כיס וכמו מרזב:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:7:3.english: Babylonian pockets - [This means] that they lift their garments off the ground when they are long, and fold it upward — *fronces* (pleats) — and hold them [in place] by means of cords, and this is like a kind of pocket and like a spout.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:8:2.hebrew: הכי מאי - קולט חלוקו (בפניו) בענין אחד ושואלו: כגון זה מרזב או לא? וחוזר וקולטו בענין אחר ושואלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:8:2.english: What [is the law] like this? - [Rabbi Yirmeya] gathers up his shirt (before him) in one manner and asks him: Is something like this [considered] a spout or not? And he again gathers it up in another manner and asks him.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:8:3.english: To gather - So that it be permanently fixed to maintain its fold forever.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:8:5.hebrew: מתנאה בסדינו - אחר שנתעטף, היה מתקנו על גופו ומיישבו. ובחול קאמר, כלומר, אלמא דאורחיה בהכי, וה"ה לשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:8:5.english: Beautifying himself with his garment - After he had wrapped himself [in it], he would arrange it on his body and settle it in place. And [this] is speaking of a weekday; that is to say, thus [we see] that such is his [normal] way [of wearing it], and the same applies on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:9:1.english: The two sides of his cloak - Which [are] on his right and on his left, toward the ground.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:9:2.hebrew: בן זירוז בזו לא חייב ר"מ חטאת - בתמיה, דאין זה דרך מלבוש אלא דרך משוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:9:2.english: Ben Zeiruz: In this [case], did Rabbi Meir not obligate a sin-offering? - [Asked] in astonishment, for this is not the manner of wearing [a garment], but rather the manner of [carrying] a burden.

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:9:3.hebrew: דקדק ר"מ ע"כ - בתמיה, לחייב חטאת בדבר הדומה להיות מותר כזה, שאינה מקופלת ואחוריה נופלין למטה מכתפיו, אלא שצידיה היו מונחין על כתפו:
Rashi on Shabbat 147a:9:3.english: Was Rabbi Meir exacting to that [extent] - [This is said] in astonishment: to obligate [one to bring] a sin-offering for something that appears to be permitted like this, where it is not folded and its back hangs down below his shoulders, rather [only] its sides were resting on his shoulder?

Rashi on Shabbat 147a:9:4.english: He lowered - He brought it down, for he accepted his words.

Tosafot on Shabbat 147a:13:1.hebrew: אף מי מערה חמין - שהוחמו באור, דאי בחמי טבריא, שרי לכתחילה, כדאמר בפרק כירה (שבת ד' מ. ושם): "והניחו להן חמי טבריא", ובפרק שמונה שרצים (ד' קט. ושם:):
Tosafot on Shabbat 147a:13:1.english: So too the cave water is hot - [This refers to water] that was heated by fire, for if [it were] like the hot springs of Tiberias, it would be permitted ab initio, as [the Gemara] says in Perek Kirah (Shabbat 40a, and there): "and they left them the hot springs of Tiberias," and in Perek Shemonah Sheratzim (109a, and 109b).

Tosafot on Shabbat 147a:13:2.hebrew: דיעבד אין - אמי מערה קאי, ולא תנא במתני' חמי טבריא אלא למידק: אף מי מערה חמין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 147a:13:2.english: After the fact, yes - [This] refers to cave water, and [the tanna] taught "hot springs of Tiberias" in the Mishnah only to infer [that] cave water is also hot.

Tosafot on Shabbat 147a:1:1.hebrew: המנער טליתו - פי' ר"ח: מן הטל שעליו, דהיינו כיבוס וליבון — חייב חטאת, וכן משמע דהוי דומיא דכומתא דרב יוסף; אבל בניעור מן העפר, כדפירש בקונטרס, אין נראה שיהא שייך ליבון:
Tosafot on Shabbat 147a:1:1.english: One who shakes his cloak - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: [Shaking it] from the dew that is upon it — which is laundering and whitening — [is why] he is liable for a sin-offering, and so it is implied, as it is similar to Rav Yosef's cap. However, regarding shaking [it] from dust, as Rashi explained, it does not appear that whitening is applicable.

Tosafot on Shabbat 147a:4:1.hebrew: היוצא בטלית מקופלת - איידי דאיירינן במי שנשרו כליו בדרך, שאז דרך הוא לקפל טליתו, נקטיה הכא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 147a:4:1.english: One who goes out with a folded cloak - Since we are dealing with one whose garments fell [into water] on the road, when it is usual to fold one's cloak, [the Gemara] cited it here:

Tosafot on Shabbat 147a:5:1.hebrew: הרטנין - רטנין כמו הרהטנין (הערוך פי' הרצים):
Tosafot on Shabbat 147a:5:1.english: Haratanin - Ratanin is like harahatanin (the Arukh explained [it as] "the runners"):

Tosafot on Shabbat 147a:7:1.hebrew: מהו לעשות מרזב - נראה לרבי דלענין איסור הוצאה איירי, כמו טלית של ד' כנפו': ולוקח שני צידי רוחב טליתו של צד ימינו, ונותן על כתף השמאלית, ואינו פושטו על כתף, אלא מקופל ומונח על כתפו. והיינו דקאמר: "מאי מרזב? כיסי בבלייתא", שקורין פרונצדר"ה; דכשהוא מונח כמו שפירשתי, יש בו כיסים מרובים, וכל כיסא וכיסא נראה כמין מרזב. ומיבעיא ליה אי איכא איסור הוצאה בכך, כיון שאינה דרך מלבוש. והיינו דקאמר: "כל אדעתא לכנופי — אסור", דהיינו כמו שפירשתי, ששני צידי הימין מקובצים ומונחים על כתף השמאלית, שיכול לילך במהרה ולא יכביד עליו טליתו. "אדעתא דלהתנאות — שפיר דמי", והיינו כשאין צידי טליתו מקובצין, אלא צד אחד מונחת על כתפו אצל צוארו, וצד האחר נופל על שכמו עד הזרוע, ואין בו שום כיסוי. והיינו "שלשל רבי טליתו" דבסמוך — שלשל אותו כמו שפירשתי, כעין להתנאות, והיינו דרך מלבוש. וכן פירש בערוך ערך מרזב: "אסור לעשות מרזב בשבת — פירוש: כשיעטוף אדם טליתו ויקפיל שני קצותיו כעין דרך קיפול ויניחנה על שכמו השמאלית, ויחזור ויקפל שאר הטלית שבצד הימין ויניחנה בכתפו". רק מה שפירש שקורין מרזב מה שטליתו מושפלת מהנה ומהנה וחלל כנגד השדרה, דנראה כמין מרזב — אינו נראה לרבי, דא"כ, מאי קאמר בתר הכי: "מאי מרזב? כיסי בבלייתא"? הלא אינו עשוי כעין כיסא! מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 147a:7:1.english: What is [the halakha as to] making a spout? - It appears to the Rabbi that [the Gemara] is speaking with regard to the prohibition of carrying out [on Shabbat], like a four-cornered cloak: one takes the two sides of the width of his cloak on his right side and places [them] on the left shoulder, and he does not spread it out over [his] shoulder, but rather [it is] folded and resting on his shoulder. And this is what [the Gemara] says: "What is a spout? Babylonian pockets," which they call froncedura [pleats]; for when it is placed as I have explained, there are many pockets in it, and each and every pocket looks like a kind of spout. And [the household] asked him whether there is a prohibition of carrying out in this, since it is not the [normal] manner of wearing [a garment]. And this is what [the Gemara] says: "Any [fold] with the intention to gather is prohibited" — that is, as I have explained, that the two sides of the right [half] are gathered and placed on the left shoulder, so that he can walk quickly and his cloak will not weigh heavily upon him. "[Any fold] with the intention to beautify oneself is permitted" — and this is when the sides of his cloak are not gathered, but rather one side rests on his shoulder near his neck, and the other side falls over his shoulder down to the arm, and there is no pocket in it. And this is [what is meant by] "Rabbi lowered his cloak" nearby [in the Gemara] — he lowered it as I have explained, in the manner of beautifying oneself, and that is the [normal] manner of wearing [a garment]. And so [too] did the Arukh explain under the entry marzev: "It is prohibited to make a spout on Shabbat — explanation: when a person wraps himself in his cloak and folds its two ends in the manner of folding and places it on his left shoulder, and goes back and folds the rest of the cloak that is on the right side and places it on his shoulder." Only what [the Arukh] explained, that they call "a spout" that which his cloak hangs down on this side and that side with a hollow opposite the spine, so that it looks like a kind of spout — this does not appear [correct] to the Rabbi, for if so, what does [the Gemara] say afterward: "What is a spout? Babylonian pockets"? Surely it is not made like a pocket! [From] my teacher.
